title: Global Hom tensor comparison normalized to the original derived counit
statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes, with the shared derived-category localizations [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Let ε₀ be the counit extracted from the same original witness that defines derivedPullback f, with its underived functor identified with module tensor pullback by the recorded object and map equalities. Let εc be the composition counit [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition], and let δ be the unique derived-functor isomorphism satisfying δ(Qh P) ≫ ε₀(P) = εc(P). Transport the canonical tensor comparison [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison] by δ inverse on its input and δ tensor δ on its outputs. This natural tensor isomorphism satisfies IsSchemeHomOriginalCounitTensorComparison: on every K-flat pair its chain isomorphism is the canonical module tensor map on every total-complex summand, and its localization equation uses ε₀ on the tensor total and each tensor factor. It is natural in both derived-category arguments. This is a partial repair: the legacy global Hom entry points still use the composition presentation pending coordinated base-change normalization.

source.place: Tags 06YJ and 079U; original presentation and transport of the K-flat total tensor comparison

proof.text: Extract the trailing original presentation without changing its proposition. Proof irrelevance identifies the choices with the original witness. Its object and map equalities identify the underived functor with module tensor pullback. Map this equality to homotopy categories and whisker with Qh; transport the counit and its universal property along the resulting explicit isomorphism.

Use exists_schemeHomTensorPullbackIso from [lem-pc-global-hom-adjunction], whose canonical predicate is proved by the monoidal realization. The universal left-derived property gives the unique isomorphism δ from εc to ε₀. Its factorization equation gives δ(Qh P) ≫ ε₀(P) = εc(P). Conjugate the existing tensor iso by δ inverse and the tensor square of δ. Precompose the old K-flat coordinate equation with δ on the input. Naturality moves δ through the localization tensor map, and the three factorization equations replace the three counits. Cancel δ followed by δ inverse. The same chain isomorphism satisfies the unchanged summand formula; naturality follows from the composite natural iso.
